# http-public test environment

A container stack to bring up the multi-tenant `http-public` mode on a public host and try it, including with the Claude connector: Postgres, Keycloak (realm imported), the app, and optionally a Caddy TLS proxy with automatic Let's Encrypt certificates. It is a test environment, not a production deployment (local KEK, one replica, one host). Background: README sections "http-public", "Keycloak setup for the Claude connector" and "Reverse proxy" in the repository README, and SPEC 5.3 and 5.7.

The operator's view (what to provide, checks in order, unverified assumptions) is in [`doc/DEPLOYMENT.md`](../../doc/DEPLOYMENT.md).

Upstream OAuth for Gmail and Microsoft 365 is not part of this environment; see [Upstream OAuth (experimental, unverified)](../../README.md#upstream-oauth-experimental-unverified) in the repository README.

It works with `docker compose`, `podman compose` (docker-compose provider) and `podman-compose`. Below, `compose` stands for the one you use.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `compose.yaml` | `postgres`, `keycloak`, `app`; `caddy` only with `--profile proxy` |
| `Dockerfile` | app image (Temurin 25 JRE, uid 10001, only the jar) |
| `setup.sh` | generates `.env` and `app/config.yaml`; with `--local` a local CA and truststore |
| `.env.example` | placeholders only; the real `.env` is generated and never committed |
| `config.yaml.example` | template of `app/config.yaml` (secrets as `env:` references only) |
| `keycloak/import/imap-mcp-realm.json` | realm `imap-mcp`: clients, scopes, mappers, no users |
| `caddy/public`, `caddy/local` | Caddyfile of the public and of the local-CA variant (`CADDY_SITE`) |
| `caddy/capture.caddy`, `tools/Redact.java` | opt-in session recording kit, see "Recording a connector session" |
| `postgres-init/` | creates the databases `keycloak` and `imapmcp` and their owners |

Images are pinned by digest (Keycloak, Postgres and Temurin as in the integration tests). The three secrets files `.env`, `app/config.yaml` and everything generated by `--local` are in `.gitignore`.

## Prerequisites

- Two DNS names pointing to the host: `MCP_HOST` (this server) and `IDP_HOST` (Keycloak). Two names keep the origins apart, so Keycloak pages cannot touch the cookies of `/accounts`.
- Inbound 80 and 443 (Let's Encrypt validates on both), outbound 443 (ACME, IdP) and 993 or 143 (your IMAP server).
- An email address for ACME.
- A built jar. Either the released 0.5.0 jar, or build it: `mvn -B -q -pl imap-mcp-app -am package -DskipTests` and copy `imap-mcp-app/target/imap-mcp-app-<version>-all.jar` to `dist/docker/jar/imap-mcp.jar`. The jar needs Java 25; it runs only on the image's runtime.
- Rootless podman: binding 80 and 443 needs `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=80` (a system setting you make yourself), or forward 80 to `HTTP_PORT` and 443 to `HTTPS_PORT` (for example 8081 and 8443) with firewalld or nftables and set both in `.env`. Open the ports in firewalld.

## Public setup

```
cd dist/docker
mkdir -p jar && cp <the-jar> jar/imap-mcp.jar
MCP_HOST=mail.example.org IDP_HOST=idp.example.org ACME_EMAIL=you@example.org \
  IMAP_HOSTS=imap.example.org ./setup.sh
compose --profile proxy build app
compose --profile proxy up -d
compose ps
```

`setup.sh` writes `.env` (mode 0600; passwords are `openssl rand -hex 32`; `HANDLE_KEY_1` and `KEK_1` are base64url without padding of 32 random bytes, a separate run each) and `app/config.yaml`. It never overwrites an existing file; delete the file to regenerate it. `IMAP_HOSTS` is a comma-separated list for `ssrf.allowedHosts`; the app refuses to link any other host.

Pass `--profile proxy` explicitly (do not rely on `COMPOSE_PROFILES` with podman-compose). A realm is imported once: to change the hostnames later, `compose down -v` (deletes all data) and regenerate `.env`, `app/config.yaml` and the Caddy certificates.

The compose network uses the default subnet `172.28.0.0/24`. If it collides with one of yours, set `BACKEND_SUBNET` (an IPv4 CIDR) in `.env`, or pass it to `setup.sh`; it feeds both `networks.backend` and `KC_PROXY_TRUSTED_ADDRESSES`.

Keycloak needs about three minutes on a first start (Postgres, then Keycloak, then the app wait on health). `compose logs -f app` shows nothing but the JVM notice: the app logs to `/logs/imap-mcp.log` in the `imap-mcp-logs` volume (`compose exec app tail -n 50 /logs/imap-mcp.log`).

### Without Caddy

Use your own TLS proxy and omit `--profile proxy`. It must:

- terminate TLS for both names and proxy `MCP_HOST` to `app:8080` (published on `127.0.0.1:${APP_PORT}`) and `IDP_HOST` to `keycloak:8080` (add a loopback port mapping for it);
- forward on `MCP_HOST` only `/mcp`, `/accounts`, `/accounts/*` and the two `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` paths; answer 404 for everything else (`/health` stays internal);
- on `IDP_HOST` answer 404 for `/admin`, `/metrics`, `/health`, `/realms/master`, `/realms/<realm>/clients-registrations` and `/realms/<realm>/account`;
- forward `Host` unchanged and set `X-Forwarded-For`, `-Proto` and `-Host` (Keycloak trusts the compose subnet `172.28.0.0/24`; set `BACKEND_SUBNET` if it collides, and adjust `KC_PROXY_TRUSTED_ADDRESSES` if your proxy is elsewhere);
- not buffer or compress responses (streaming), allow upstream reads above `tools.deadline` (default 90 s), and cap request bodies above `http.maxRequestBytes` (1 MiB);
- keep no access log with query strings (the OAuth callback carries codes).

The app itself fetches discovery and JWKS from `https://<IDP_HOST>/...` and validates the certificate, so the app container must resolve `IDP_HOST` to the proxy with a valid certificate (an `extra_hosts` entry, or your own network alias).

## First user

The admin console is never public. Create the first user inside the Keycloak container with kcadm. Use a real terminal (kcadm prompts for passwords and refuses without one; do not use `-T`); passwords are never on the command line. The bootstrap admin is `bootstrap-admin`, its password is `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `.env`.

```
K="compose exec keycloak /opt/keycloak/bin/kcadm.sh"
$K config credentials --config /tmp/kcadm.config --server http://localhost:8080 --realm master --user bootstrap-admin
$K create users --config /tmp/kcadm.config -r imap-mcp -s username=owner -s enabled=true \
  -s email=you@example.org -s emailVerified=true -s firstName=Owner -s lastName=Test \
  -s 'requiredActions=["CONFIGURE_TOTP"]'
$K set-password --config /tmp/kcadm.config -r imap-mcp --username owner
$K add-roles --config /tmp/kcadm.config -r imap-mcp --uusername owner --rolename imap-mcp-user
compose exec keycloak rm /tmp/kcadm.config
```

The realm requires a password of at least 14 characters. Without the role `imap-mcp-user` the first login to `/accounts` is refused with 403.

## Claude connector

In Claude: Customize, Connectors, Add custom connector.

- URL exactly `https://<MCP_HOST>/mcp`.
- Advanced settings: client id `claude-connector`, client secret blank. Authentication settings cannot be edited afterwards; remove and re-add the connector to change them.
- The realm closes dynamic client registration; entering the client id is mandatory, otherwise Claude tries registration and fails.
- The redirect URI `https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback` is registered; `https://claude.com/api/mcp/auth_callback` is registered as an assumption. Claude Code is not covered.

Opening dynamic client registration for Claude is possible but not set up here: it needs an IP allowlist of Anthropic's published range in Caddy for the registration endpoint, the Trusted Hosts policy limited to `claude.ai` and `claude.com`, the Allowed Client Scopes policy limited to `imap-mcp:read` and `imap-mcp:write`, and a low Max Clients.

## Owner checklist

0. Preflight (replace the names): `dig +short <MCP_HOST> <IDP_HOST>`; `compose logs caddy` shows both certificates issued; then
   - `curl -s https://<IDP_HOST>/realms/imap-mcp/.well-known/openid-configuration` shows `issuer` equal to `oauth.issuer` and every endpoint on `https://<IDP_HOST>`;
   - `curl -s https://<MCP_HOST>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` shows `resource` `https://<MCP_HOST>/mcp`;
   - `curl -si -X POST https://<MCP_HOST>/mcp` answers 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ... resource_metadata=...`;
   - `/admin/`, `/realms/master/...` and `/realms/imap-mcp/clients-registrations/...` on `<IDP_HOST>` answer 404, and so does `/health` on `<MCP_HOST>`;
   - no "OIDC discovery failed" in `/logs/imap-mcp.log`.
1. Create the first user (above).
2. Browser: `https://<MCP_HOST>/accounts`, log in, set up TOTP; the callback creates the tenant. A user without the role gets 403.
3. Link a mail account with `read_only` on; a host outside `IMAP_HOSTS` is refused.
4. Claude connector: the consent screen lists read and write; the connector shows as connected.
5. Read tools work and leave messages unread (PEEK); keep a chat going for more than 5 minutes so the access token refreshes.
6. Write tools: `read_only` refuses them; turn `read_only` off; `set_flags`, move and delete to Trash then work, and audit rows exist.
7. Only now consider `http.stateful: true` and `purge.enabled: true` in `app/config.yaml` (`compose restart app`), then the v3b smoke checklist of the repository README.
8. Teardown.

`http.allowedOrigins` is left at its default. Observed (deployed tests): without an `Origin` header the request passes, and `https://claude.ai` is refused with 403; with `http.allowedOrigins: ["https://claude.ai"]` and a restart it passes. Whether Claude sends an `Origin` header, and which, is not verified. If `/mcp` answers 403 at Claude's first request, set `http.allowedOrigins: ["https://claude.ai"]` in `app/config.yaml` and restart the app.

The realm rotates refresh tokens (`revokeRefreshToken` true, `refreshTokenMaxReuse` 0). Observed: reusing an old refresh token revokes the session, and two refreshes with the same token at the same moment usually leave the client logged out. If Claude reconnects sporadically, the recommendation (not tested) is to keep rotation and raise `refreshTokenMaxReuse` to 1 (Realm settings, Tokens). The details are in section 4 of [DEPLOYMENT.md](../../doc/DEPLOYMENT.md).

## Recording a connector session

Records one real Claude connector session as a test fixture. The production Caddyfiles have no access log on purpose (the OAuth callback carries codes in the query string); `caddy/capture.caddy` is an opt-in snippet that logs with the secrets removed, and `tools/Redact.java` converts the log into the fixture format by allowlist (format: `ConnectorSessionFixture` in `imap-mcp-it`, directory `imap-mcp-it/src/test/resources/connector/`). The kit works on the public variant. Run all commands in `dist/docker`.

1. Do the `/accounts` login first (browser, TOTP) so that the capture starts with the connector's own requests.
2. Make a working copy of the snippet in the Caddy directory and import it: `cp caddy/capture.caddy caddy/public/`; in `caddy/public/Caddyfile` add `import capture.caddy` as the first line and `import capture` as the first line inside both site blocks. Restart Caddy: `compose --profile proxy restart caddy`.
3. In Claude, connect the connector, run one tool call, then wait more than 5 minutes (past one access token refresh) and run another.
4. Remove the snippet at once: `rm caddy/public/capture.caddy`, undo the three added lines in `caddy/public/Caddyfile` (`git checkout caddy/public/Caddyfile`), restart Caddy.
5. Copy the log out of the volume (it is mode 0600) into a private directory: `umask 077; d=$(mktemp -d)`, then `compose --profile proxy cp caddy:/data/capture/connector.log $d/connector.log`, and delete it in the container: `compose --profile proxy exec caddy rm -r /data/capture`.
6. Convert (needs Java 25 or later; the host names are those of `.env`): `MCP_HOST=<MCP_HOST> IDP_HOST=<IDP_HOST> java tools/Redact.java $d/connector.log session.jsonl`. A malformed line, a line that is no access entry or an unknown host fails the conversion and writes nothing. Then `shred -u $d/connector.log; rmdir $d`.
7. Review `session.jsonl` by eye before anything is committed. The backend `User-Agent` is kept verbatim; whether a recorded one is committed is an open owner decision, so check this field in particular. Hosts appear as `<MCP_HOST>` and `<IDP_HOST>`, query values only for `response_type`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`, `resource`, `code_challenge_method` and `prompt`.

Keycloak events of the same period (type, client, error and the redirect URI, grant type, scope and reason, without IP, user, session, code and token ids). Use a real terminal, as in "First user":

```
K="compose exec keycloak /opt/keycloak/bin/kcadm.sh"
$K config credentials --config /tmp/kcadm.config --server http://localhost:8080 --realm master --user bootstrap-admin
$K get events --config /tmp/kcadm.config -r imap-mcp -q max=500 \
  | jq 'sort_by(.time) | (.[0].time) as $t0 | map({type, clientId, error, relativeMs: (.time - $t0),
      redirect_uri: .details.redirect_uri, grant_type: .details.grant_type, scope: .details.scope, reason: .details.reason})' \
  > keycloak-events.json
```

Review `keycloak-events.json` too; the raw events never leave the pipe.

## Local trial without DNS

`./setup.sh --local` uses the names `mail.imap-mcp.test` and `idp.imap-mcp.test` on port 8443 with a local CA (`local-ca/`, a throwaway CA; its key stays there), a leaf certificate for both names (`caddy/local/certs/`) and a truststore for the app (`truststore/truststore.p12`: the JDK's default CAs plus the local CA, built in the Temurin image with the container engine). It needs no DNS entries and no outbound ACME:

```
./setup.sh --local
compose --profile proxy up -d
curl --cacert local-ca/ca.crt --resolve idp.imap-mcp.test:8443:127.0.0.1 \
  https://idp.imap-mcp.test:8443/realms/imap-mcp/.well-known/openid-configuration
```

Browsers need the two names in `/etc/hosts` pointing to 127.0.0.1 and the CA imported; `curl --resolve` needs neither. The Claude connector cannot reach a local setup.

## Operations and teardown

- `compose --profile proxy down` stops and removes the containers; data stays in the named volumes (`postgres-data`, `imap-mcp-logs`, `caddy-data`, `caddy-config`).
- `compose --profile proxy down -v` also deletes the volumes: databases, the imported realm, users, linked accounts and the certificates (Let's Encrypt rate limits apply to re-issuing).
- Upgrade the jar: replace `jar/imap-mcp.jar`, `compose build app`, `compose up -d app`. Flyway migrates at startup.
- Do not print `compose config` (it expands secrets); validate with `compose config -q`.

## Podman notes

- `podman-compose` needs a recent version for `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` (1.6.0 worked; check older versions yourself). `podman compose` uses the docker-compose provider; for it enable the socket: `systemctl --user enable --now podman.socket`.
- Rootless healthchecks need systemd user timers: enable linger (`loginctl enable-linger $USER`), or containers show no health state.
- podman ignores the Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK`; `compose.yaml` repeats every healthcheck.
- Bind mounts carry `:Z` (SELinux relabel) and are directories, not single files. Never add `:Z` to a home directory or to the repository root.
- Do not use `keep-id`: it breaks Postgres and Keycloak, which need their own uids; writable data is in named volumes.
- Image names are fully qualified (Fedora's short-name enforcement); the built image is `localhost/imap-mcp-public:dev`.
